newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Moody's says HSBC no threat to Brazil retail banks.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says HSBC no threat to Brazil retail banks.

text.p: Brazilian retail banks should not fear competition from HSBC Holdings Plc after the takeover of Brazil's fourth largest private bank, a senior analyst at Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday.

Francisco Abreu said local banks are well prepared to compete with the Anglo-Asian financial conglomerate, which moved to strenghten its presence in Brazil by acquiring selected assets and obligations of Banco Bamerindus.
Brazilian banks may have been caught by surprise with HSBC's acquisition of Bamerindus, but Abreu sees no difficulties for local banks in facing the new player.
"Brazilian banks have all the conditions to compete with foreign banks," he told reporters, before speaking at a seminar on banking risk in Brazil and Latin America.
The major challenge for Brazil banks is to reduce costs to compete with the new player.
He also said HSBC's entry into the Brazilian market will lead other foreign financial institutions to think about opportunities in the banking sector.
Brazil could follow the example of Venezuela, which now has one of Latin America's best financial systems, attracting great foreign interest, he added.
"Nobody expected that Venezuela would draw foreign capital so fast," he said.
The Moody's analyst, however, pointed out that foreigners could enter Brazil's banking sector at slower pace because the Brazilian system is not as transparent as Venezuela's.
He said Brazilian banks, for example, have to improve the disclosure and publication of their balance sheets.
Abreu also said the Brazilian banking sector has been improving, adding that the country has never faced the risk of "an endemic crisis."
The analyst said Moody's will reconsider its ratings of Bamerindus after the HSBC takeover deal. He said the revaluation will take 60 days.
